Hi! I'm hitting this exact bug on **v1.18.18** (latest release) with multiple providers (OpenCode Go / DeepSeek V4 Flash, NVIDIA Nemotron, local LM Studio). During streaming, each reasoning token renders on its own line — it looks like the agent is stuck emitting one word per second. The content is correct in the data layer, only the TUI rendering is broken.

The fix is already written in PRs #36086 and #36087 but both were auto-closed by the compliance bot without merging. Could these be reopened/merged? This is affecting many users (see #27193, #25094). Thanks!

Also affected here on **v1.18.18**. With fast-streaming reasoning models (DeepSeek V4 Flash via OpenCode Go, Qwen 3.5 local), the TUI freezes/stutters badly during streaming because every message.part.delta triggers a full store mutation with no batching. Combined with #36037 (one token per line) it looks like the agent is completely stuck. A ~30-50ms debounce flush for deltas (as suggested) would help a lot. Thanks!

Environment: - OpenCode Desktop: 1.18.18 - OS: Windows - Provider: opencode-go / Console Go - Model: gpt-5.6-luna - Variant: high My Go subscription quotas are not exhausted: - Rolling: 0% - Weekly: 18% - Monthly: 11% Additional verification: - A fresh request to `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses` with the same API key succeeds with HTTP 200. - Replaying an old `reasoningEncryptedContent` stored in an affected session reproduces `invalid_encrypted_content`. - Multiple existing sessions fail, while the problem is tied to their stored Responses reasoning metadata. - The logs also show connection resets/timeouts before the encrypted-content errors. Hit this with the `atlassian-rovo-mcp` remote server (`https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2`) and traced it end to end — adding as a concrete data point since this issue doesn't currently mention Atlassian/Rovo.

**Symptom:** despite having a 90-day refresh token (`offline_access` scope, rotating), the server needed a full interactive re-auth (`opencode mcp auth atlassian-rovo-mcp`) roughly every 8 hours — i.e. exactly the access token's lifetime, as if the refresh token were never being used at all.

**Server log** (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`) shows the pattern clearly — repeated failures every 20-90 min for hours with no refresh attempt or error ever logged in between, just an immediate fall-through to `needs_auth`:

```
level=WARN message="mcp connect failed" server=atlassian-rovo-mcp status.status=needs_auth
level=WARN message="mcp connect failed" server=atlassian-rovo-mcp status.status=needs_auth
... (repeats every 20-90 min for ~12 hours)
level=INFO message="cli starting" args=["mcp","auth","atlassian-rovo-mcp"]   <- manual re-auth required
```

**Root cause appears to be upstream in the MCP TypeScript SDK.** Atlassian issues rotating refresh tokens (`"https://id.atlassian.com/atl_token_type":"ROTATING_REFRESH"` in the decoded JWT) — each refresh invalidates the old refresh token and issues a new one that must be persisted immediately. The SDK's own `auth()` helper had a bug where a `provider.saveTokens()` failure during that persistence step was silently swallowed and the client fell through to requesting a brand new authorization — exactly this symptom. Confirmed via the SDK's own changeset description:

> Against an authorization server that rotates refresh tokens... this loses credentials rather than merely hiding an error. The exchange has already succeeded server-side, so the old refresh token is invalidated at the moment the new one is issued; dropping the new token set leaves nothing usable on either side.

Fixed upstream in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2053, merged 2026-08-18 — but **not yet in any published release** (latest npm `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is still `1.30.0` from 2026-07-27, before the fix), and opencode itself currently pins `1.29.0` in `packages/opencode/package.json`, one minor behind even that.

So right now there's no available fix at either layer for OAuth servers with rotating refresh tokens (Atlassian, Keycloak, and per the SDK changeset this is "the OAuth 2.1 default"). Once the SDK cuts a release containing #2053, opencode will also need to bump its `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` dependency past `1.29.0`/`1.30.0` to pick it up.

Independent reproduction / cross-provider control:

- Endpoint: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`
- Model: `deepseek-v4-flash`
- Authentication: active OpenCode Go API key
- Transport: direct HTTPS (proxy environment cleared), `User-Agent: OpenCode/1.0`

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| no `tools` | `200 OK` (`OK`) |
| 21 minimal, valid OpenAI function schemas | `400 [unsupported_tool_schema] ... (tool_count_limit)` |

As a control, I sent the same model prompt and same 21 tool schemas directly to `https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions` using an official DeepSeek API key: both the no-tools and 21-tools requests returned `200 OK`.

This isolates the regression to the OpenCode Go / Console Go gateway rather than DeepSeek V4 Flash or a client-side schema incompatibility. It also independently confirms that the effective Go limit is below 21; the 16/17 boundary in the issue description is consistent with this result.

We root-caused this one locally — it's **not** actually a tool-count limit. It's the JSON Schema numeric-bounds keywords (`minimum` / `maximum`) being rejected by the Console Go upstream.

## Evidence (all on opencode-go + deepseek-v4-flash, real API key, direct HTTPS)

1. **Per-tool bisect**: sending a single tool at a time, only `process`, `read_file`, `terminal` each failed with the exact same `400 [unsupported_tool_schema] ... tool_count_limit`. The other 12 tools were all `200 OK` individually.
2. **Schema diff**: those 3 failing tools are the only ones carrying `minimum`/`maximum` in their parameters (e.g. `terminal.timeout: {type: integer, minimum: 1}`, `read_file.limit: {maximum: 2000}`).
3. **Decisive experiment**: send **all 15 tools** but strip every `minimum`/`maximum`/`exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum` from the schemas → `200 OK`. Re-add them → `400` again.
4. Control: the same 15-tool payload to `api.deepseek.com` works fine with min/max intact — so the schemas are valid JSON Schema; only Console Go rejects them.

This also explains the weird "16 tools OK / 17 tools 400" boundary you saw: it's not the count — it's whether the catalog happens to include one of the min/max-carrying tool definitions.

## Workaround (no need to wait for upstream)

Strip the four numeric-bounds keywords from tool schemas before sending to opencode-go:

```python
def strip_min_max(node):
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        for k in ("minimum", "maximum", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum"):
            node.pop(k, None)
        for v in node.values():
            strip_min_max(v)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for x in node:
            strip_min_max(x)
```

We patched the Hermes gateway's tool-schema sanitizer with this (it already strips `pattern`/`format`/`enum` for xAI) and `deepseek-v4-flash` + full 15-tool catalog now works end-to-end. Hopefully upstream relaxes the keyword check or the error message (which is very misleading as `tool_count_limit`), but this unblocks us regardless.

For maintainers — we identified the specific keyword family behind the `unsupported_keyword` variant of this error on opencode-go + deepseek-v4-flash (filed as #43378 too).

## Root cause (verified with real API key, direct HTTPS)

The Console Go upstream rejects JSON Schema **numeric-bounds keywords**: `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`.

Evidence:
- Per-tool bisect: only tools carrying `minimum`/`maximum` in their parameters (e.g. `terminal.timeout: {minimum: 1}`, `read_file.limit: {maximum: 2000}`) fail individually with the 400; all other tools pass alone.
- Sending the **full 15-tool catalog with min/max stripped → 200 OK**; re-adding them → 400 again.
- Same payload with min/max intact to `api.deepseek.com` → 200 OK (schemas are valid JSON Schema).

## Suggested fix upstream

Either accept these standard keywords, or — minimally — don't label this as `tool_count_limit`, which sends everyone down a "how many tools" rabbit hole. The exact keyword names are in the error payload the upstream returns; if you can surface which keyword is rejected (instead of the generic `unsupported_keyword`), clients can sanitize precisely.

Local workaround (strips the 4 keywords client-side) works fine in the meantime.

Thanks for the triage. I checked the referenced issues and believe this one is a distinct failure mode worth tracking separately, even though it shares the same underlying family (catalog entries with `variants: []` + a "medium" default).

Comparison:

- **[#40182](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/40182)**: `--variant` values outside `reasoning_options` are **silently ignored** (no error). This issue is the opposite: the TUI **persists** a `medium` variant into the session at creation and the resolver **hard-fails** with `VariantUnavailableError` at runtime.
- **[#36888](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36888)**: MiniMax-M3 with `variants: []` simply loses the `/variants` command; sessions run fine with the default. In our case the model does **not** run — the session crashes on every prompt until the variant is manually reset. This shows the `variants: []` cases are not all equal: #36888 degrades gracefully, ours fails hard.
- **[#25126](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/25126)**: display-only issue where the TUI **shows** `medium` in the badge. Ours is behavioral: the `medium` variant is **written into the session model** and then crashes resolution.

Additional severity detail: after the failure, opencode2 silently falls back to another model (`opencode/big-pickle`) — the user is switched to a different model without any visible notice, which is easy to miss.

Root cause summary: the TUI auto-pins a `medium` reasoning variant for models with `reasoning: true`, even when the catalog entry declares `variants: []`, and the resolver throws a hard `VariantUnavailableError` instead of resolving to the default.

Happy to consolidate this into any canonical issue if the maintainers prefer, but I'd suggest keeping this open as the V2 hard-error case.
